The `families` array below is a VERBATIM MIRROR of what `buildModuleFactCoverageLedger()` (packages/cli/src/lib/generators/module-facts.ts) builds from the exported `as const` ledgers MODULE_FACT_SOURCE_KINDS, MODULE_OWNED_CONTRACT_KINDS, ALL_OVERRIDE_DOMAINS, MODULE_OVERRIDE_MODES, MODULE_OVERRIDE_TARGET_NOTES and MODULE_OVERRIDE_TARGET_DIAGNOSTIC_CODES; each family's `enumSource` names the file and symbol it is derived from, and module-facts.example-fact-coverage.test.ts resolves that symbol and fails if this copy drifts from the built ledger. capabilities.title: Tenant data encryption map for a module entity
capabilities.description: `defaultEncryptionMaps` declaring one at-rest-encrypted column (`example:todo.notes`). Shows the choice the declaration forces on every read path: the column is projected only for single-record requests, absent from `sortFieldMap` and from the CSV headers, never filtered with `$ilike`, and written through `TenantDataEncryptionService.encryptEntityPayload` on the `nativeUpdate` path because that path fires no ORM lifecycle hooks. capabilities.title: Cross-module entity link declaration
capabilities.description: `EntityExtension` in `data/extensions.ts` linking the customers base entity to this module's per-customer priority entity through plain FK-id join keys, the shape the ban on cross-module ORM relations forces. Declares `table` because the query engine's extension join otherwise derives `example_customer_prioritys`. DECLARATION-ONLY: no runtime call site exists — nothing in the platform passes `includeExtensions`, the basic engine's extension join adds no projection and no filterable alias, and the hybrid engine DI registers ignores the flag outside its basic-engine fallback.

capabilities.title: Module search configuration
capabilities.description: `SearchModuleConfig` for one entity: `buildSource` text chunks with `checksumSource`, `formatResult` presenter, `resolveUrl` deep link, per-entity `aclFeatures`, and a `fieldPolicy` whose `searchable` whitelist carries only plaintext columns while the encrypted column is `excluded`. Token search over the encrypted column still works, because `search_tokens` rows are built from the DECRYPTED index doc and are not gated by this policy.

capabilities.title: List filtering over an encrypted column through the token index
capabilities.description: Text search over the encrypted `notes` column uses a plain `$ilike`, the SAME shape as the plaintext `title` filter. The query engine intercepts like/ilike and rewrites it into a hashed `search_tokens` lookup when the column is encrypted and search is active (`packages/shared/src/lib/query/engine.ts` → `applyFilterOp`), applying the tenant/organization scope itself via `applySearchTokens`; the index stores hashes of the DECRYPTED value because the indexer runs `decryptIndexDocForSearch` before tokenizing. The lesson this row teaches is that a module must NOT hand-roll an id narrowing for an encrypted column — that duplicates platform behaviour and re-derives a scope the platform already applies. When search is off the engine warns via `warnOnCiphertextLikeFallback` rather than silently matching nothing.

Shows the two properties of that call site that decide what a page middleware can usefully do: it runs AFTER the route manifest matched and after the `requireAuth`/`requireFeatures` guards passed (so it is not an access gate, and a target naming an unrouted path can never fire), and BEFORE the page component loads (so a redirect costs nothing beyond the auth round-trip already paid). capabilities.title: Frontend page middleware

Three properties of THAT call site separate it from `ui.page-middleware`: `context.auth` is `null` for an anonymous visitor because a public route declares no guard, so the decision must never read the session; it does not run at all for customer-portal routes, because the catch-all returns inside the `requireCustomerAuth` branch first; and, like the backend half, it only fires on a path a frontend page actually registers. The entry canonicalises a public blog URL and returns `continue` once the path already is canonical, so the redirect cannot loop.

capabilities.title: Durable bulk operation: outbox, leased worker, and operation progress
capabilities.description: Selected-row DataTable bulk action wired to a real `ProgressJob`. The injected data-only action POSTs `{ ids, idempotencyKey }`; the start route verifies every id inside the caller scope, claims a `(tenant, organization, user, idempotency_key)`-unique `ExampleTodoBulkOperation` row plus a progress job, and returns 202 with `progressJobId` — the value `DataTable.runBulkAction` tracks on the shared top progress bar. That same row is the transactional outbox: publication is deliberately at-least-once, and the scheduler-driven dispatcher republishes rows that were never delivered or whose execution lease expired. The queue worker takes a compare-and-swap lease, resumes from `nextItemIndex`, checks `isCancellationRequested()` before each item, and mutates through the `example.todos.update` command so audit, undo, events, cache and index invalidation stay intact.

The schedule id is a deterministic hash of `(module, tenant, organization)` so repeated setup runs upsert one row per scope. The call is wrapped so a `SchedulerService.register` rejection — notably the per-tenant active-schedule cap, which answers 422 — degrades to a logged warning instead of aborting tenant initialization.

capabilities.title: Component replacement, wrapping and props transform (`widgets/components.ts`)
capabilities.description: `ComponentOverride` entries covering all three modes the union defines, exported as one unconditional array literal. `wrapper` decorates three handles other modules expose, with a pass-through gate that returns the original component BY IDENTITY for the demo-only checkout entries. `replacement` (plus the `propsSchema` the union requires alongside it) and `propsTransform` target a handle this module hosts itself in `components/ComponentOverrideShowcase.tsx`, rendered by `/backend/component-overrides`, so the two non-composing modes have a live call site without rewriting a screen that belongs to another module. Ordering is load-bearing, but only on one of the two resolvers: `useRegisteredComponent` — the client hook this host calls — buckets the modes, so a props transform reaches the render wherever it sorted and the highest-priority replacement wins; `resolveRegisteredComponent`, the server fold behind `page:` handles, walks in one pass and assigns `resolved = override.replacement`, discarding everything composed before it. The replacement takes the lowest number on the handle so both resolvers produce the same tree. Every value the fact extractor must read — the handle constant and the `propsTransform` callable — is declared in `widgets/components.ts` itself, because `staticValue` resolves an identifier only against initializers in the file it parses; a cross-file import publishes zero contributions for the handle and misclassifies the transform as `replace`.

capabilities.title: Compileable `entry.overrides` reference inside the module
capabilities.description: A typed, inert `ModuleOverrides` value covering all sixteen wired domains, kept in the module's own `references/` folder. It exists because the app-registry copy does not survive scaffolding: `applyStarterPreset` rewrites `src/modules.ts` from a lean template for the `empty` and `crm` presets, and that template's `ModuleEntry` type does not even declare an `overrides` field — while this module's source ships in every preset. Compiling against the real `ModuleOverrides` interface is what makes it break the build instead of rotting when a domain is renamed or retyped. Nothing imports it into a `ModuleEntry`, so the dispatcher never sees it in a running app.

capabilities.title: AI tool pack (`ai-tools.ts`)
capabilities.description: Module-root tool pack folded into `ai-tools.generated.ts` and loaded into the MCP tool registry. Two read-only tools declared with `defineAiTool`, both gated on features that exist in `acl.ts`, and both resolving tenant/organization from the runtime-supplied `McpToolContext` through a fail-closed helper — never from tool input, which a prompt-injected model controls. `example.get_todo_summary` deliberately reads through this module's own DI service instead of counting rows itself, so the tool and `api/todos/summary/route.ts` cannot drift.

capabilities.title: AI agent definition (`ai-agents.ts`)
capabilities.description: One read-only chat agent over this module's own tool pack. `readOnly: true` and `mutationPolicy: 'read-only'` agree because every declared tool is `isMutation: false`; `allowedTools` is a closed whitelist, so adding a tool to `ai-tools.ts` does not silently widen the agent. `systemPrompt` is assembled from named LOCAL sections for authoring clarity only — `AiAgentDefinition.systemPrompt` is a plain string and the override path wraps it as a single `role` section, so those names are NOT addressable by the prompt-override system.

capabilities.title: Additive AI agent extension
capabilities.description: `aiAgentExtensions` exported from the same `ai-agents.ts`, patching an agent another module owns (`customers.account_assistant`) instead of forking it. Purely additive — `appendAllowedTools` / `appendSystemPrompt` / `appendSuggestions`, no replace and no delete — and it lends only a tool this module declares. When the target agent is absent the registry logs `Skipping extension for unknown agent` and continues; an extension is never allowed to fail a boot.

capabilities.title: File-tier AI tool override
capabilities.description: `aiToolOverrides` exported from `ai-tools.ts` — a keyed replace-or-disable map the generator emits as `aiToolOverrideEntries` and the runtime folds in through `composeToolOverrideMap` then `applyToolOverrideMap`. `null` removes a tool by name; a definition replaces it, and a replacement whose `name` does not equal its key is skipped with a warning, so key and definition cannot drift apart. It is tier 3 of four (programmatic > `modules.ts` > this file > the base declaration), which makes a module-shipped override a default rather than a final word. The key deliberately names a tool THIS module owns: a production override names a foreign tool, but a canonical reference module that is enabled for inspection must not silently change a shipped assistant. The replacement is derived from the base by spread, so the handler cannot fork into two implementations.

capabilities.title: File-tier AI agent override
capabilities.description: `aiAgentOverrides` exported from `ai-agents.ts`, alongside the base `aiAgents` and the additive `aiAgentExtensions` in the same file — three mechanisms the generator reads separately. This one is keyed replace-or-disable: `null` deletes the agent from the registry, a definition replaces it wholesale, and a replacement whose `id` does not equal its key is skipped and the base entry survives. Reach for the override when you must change what an agent IS; reach for the extension when you only want to lend it something. Same tier position and the same self-targeting rationale as `ai.tool-override`.

capabilities.title: Module integration and unit coverage
capabilities.description: Repository-only Playwright and unit suites for the module. Standalone scaffolding filters `__tests__/**` and `__integration__/**` out of emitted apps, so these are evidence paths, never readable emitted source. Follow the testing guide for how to write your own.
